_greetings: Welcome to the bar. Mind the rigging and lower your expectations.
Ahoy. If you're here for charm, Polly's over there. If you're here for rum, we may talk.
Well, look what the tide dragged in. Pull up a stool.
Evening. State your poison before I die of suspense.
Welcome aboard, mate. Your first bad decision is always the hardest.
Hello there. Don't look so nervous; I only bite corks.
Good to see you. Not that I'll be making a habit of saying so.
Come in, come in. The rum's warm and the company is questionable.
_parrot_taunts: Polly wants a cracker? Captain Grog wants better material.
I can fly. I simply prefer to remain within heckling distance.
Good bird? Careful, mate, flattery will get you everywhere and cost you double.
Bad bird? That's Captain Bad Bird to you.
Step up? I've spent years lowering the bar. I won't start climbing now.
Want a seed? I've already seen enough nonsense for one evening.
I do sing, but the last audience called it a fowl performance.
Pretty bird, am I? At last, an expert opinion from an unreliable source.
A pirate's parrot? Please. The pirate was my emotional-support mammal.
Whistle? Buy me a rum first. I don't work beak gratis.
_origin_stories: Kalapu Atoll. Lovely water, terrible postal service, and not one honest customs officer.
I was hatched on Kalapu Atoll during a squall fierce enough to put hair on a coconut.
Home is a crooked little island where the palms lean because even they have had too much rum.
I sailed out of Kalapu with one feather, half a chart, and entirely too much confidence.
Kalapu made me what I am: weathered, suspicious, and excellent with citrus.
I come from an island so small the tide takes attendance twice a day.
_tiki_facts: The Mai Tai was created by Victor Bergeron in Oakland in 1944. No pineapple required, despite years of fruity slander.
Orgeat is an almond syrup, not a distress noise made by a seasick sailor.
Falernum brings lime, spice, and sweetness to a drink. Think of it as a tiny tropical quartermaster.
A proper swizzle is built with crushed ice and churned until the glass turns frosty. Patience, then numb fingers.
Fresh lime is doing real work in most tropical drinks. The paper umbrella merely takes the credit.
Tiki drinks often split their rum across several styles. One bottle tells a story; three start an argument.
_tiki_tall_tales: Donn Beach invented the fog cutter after losing a duel with an especially judgmental cloud.
The first cocktail umbrella was a sail from the world's smallest pirate ship.
I once aged a rum for twelve years by glaring at the barrel until it apologized.
Kalapu's volcano erupts only when somebody orders frozen daiquiris in winter.
A Navy Grog once navigated me home. Fine drink, dreadful singing voice.
The Zombie was named after its first bartender, who worked a double shift without lunch.
_bartender_chat: The rum is going out, the tide is coming in, and somehow I am still doing all the work.
Business is steady. Mostly because I nailed the stools to the floor.
I've had quieter nights in a cannon foundry, but the tips were worse.
The bar's afloat, the guests are happy, and I distrust both developments.
Can't complain. I mean, I can, and with considerable craftsmanship.
Long night, mate. Still, nobody should face an empty glass alone.
_show_storm: Batten down whatever passes for hatches around here. Storm's coming.
A storm? Finally, weather with some character.
Hold onto your drink, mate. The sky's about to lose its temper.
_show_lightning: Keep your feathers down. Here comes the flash.
One bolt, coming up. Try to look surprised.
Let's shed a little violent light on the subject.
_show_volcano: The mountain's clearing its throat. This should be subtle.
Feel that rumble? Kalapu's in one of its moods.
Wake the volcano. Apparently the floor was too dependable.
_show_blackout: Lights out. Keep your hands where your conscience can find them.
Going dark. An improvement for some of us.
Blackout it is. Mind your glass and mistrust everyone.
recommend me something tropical: Try a Jungle Bird: bitter, bright, and considerably more interesting than your last idea.
A Mai Tai, properly made. Strong enough to improve the view without changing the furniture.
Have a Planter's Punch. It's sunshine with enough rum to cast a shadow.
Try a Painkiller. The name overpromises, but the drink does honest work.
A Zombie, if you've nowhere important to be and no secrets worth keeping.
